checks.reason: Direct expansion gives E W(tau tensor q)^2 = int int tau(t)tau(u)|t-u|^(-a) dt du * int Gamma(dy) int q(x)q(x-y)dx = Q_sp ||tau||_a^2. Under tau->c tau both sides scale by c^2. checks.claim: Q_sp is positive and finite, and signed temporal strict positivity via the Volterra/lambda identity gives infinitude (lines 82-111).
checks.reason: For y in B_L and x in B_(L+1), both q factors are at least 1, so Q_sp>=|B_(L+1)|Gamma(B_L)>0. Finiteness follows from compact support. I recomputed int_(-inf)^min(t,s) 2 lambda e^(-lambda(t-r)) e^(-lambda(s-r)) dr = e^(-lambda|t-s|) and the Laplace identity. Tonelli holds because the absolute form equals the finite Riesz form. Zero norm gives E_lambda=0 for some lambda, then v=0 by continuity, and v'=lambda v-tau gives tau=0. The map tau -> tau tensor q is therefore injective on an infinite-dimensional space.

checks.claim: Gram-Schmidt gives compact smooth representatives, and independence comes from orthonormality, not disjoint time supports (lines 113-119).
checks.reason: Finite combinations of tests are tests, zero residuals are discarded only in the null quotient, and density gives completeness. E g_j g_k=delta_jk plus joint Gaussianity from the linearity of W factor the characteristic functions. No time-support argument, H_W-valued white vector or negative-time noise appears.

checks.claim: The covariance coefficient (19.6)-(19.7) has the mask after K/Gamma, uses Gamma once, and has smoothness, literal real/complex identity and representative identity on t>=0 (lines 123-165).
checks.reason: (19.6) has zeta_R outside and one Gamma. Deterministic zero extension and local bounded v and compact y ranges justify moving all derivatives onto f_j under dominated integration. The covariance with x'=x-y gives (19.7) for positive-time F. Wave tests pass to the limit through the Prop 17.3 approximations, using the unmasked coefficient's boundedness on the mask support, and W_C is complex linear without a conjugate. A null difference has zero covariance with every zeta_R F, so masked coefficients agree on t>0 and at 0 by continuity. No quotient multiplier is introduced, so there is no conflict with Prop 16.5.

checks.claim: CLARIFIED: gain (19.9), strong continuity only, all-real Sobolev multipliers and the Lipschitz primitive hold, with E_(r+1)-valued continuity for each E_r input (lines 170-205).
checks.reason: Normalized off-diagonal entries are <xi>|sin(t|xi|)|/|xi|<=C_T and |xi||sin(t|xi|)|/<xi><=1 at every r. B(H(t)) maps E_r to E_(r+1) since the second entry H u lies in H^r. S(t)z is E_r continuous, multiplication is norm continuous in t, and S(-t) is strongly continuous on E_(r+1). The integrand is therefore E_(r+1)-valued continuous and uniformly bounded, giving the Bochner bound and the Lipschitz norm primitive. Norm continuity of S is not used. The v2 wording fixes the earlier note.

checks.claim: The E_s dual and adjoint gain are correct (lines 207-211).
checks.reason: The pairing identifies the dual of H^r x H^(r-1) with H^(2s-r) x H^(2s-r-1)=E_(2s-r), isometrically via Bessel weights. The adjoint therefore maps E_(2s-r-1) to E_(2s-r). checks.claim: Finite propagation covers both entries, with support-compatible density, cutoff slack and BOTH localization identities (19.10) (lines 213-228).
checks.reason: I rederived the energy derivative: it equals the boundary integral of v d_n u-(v^2+|grad u|^2)/2, which is at most 0. Velocity and gradient vanish in the cone, and time integration gives displacement zero. (1-chi)z_n converges to (1-chi)z in E_r, and these approximants vanish on B_(2R+T+1). Displacement therefore vanishes on B_(2R+1) throughout [0,T], which contains supp H, and the product is exactly zero and passes to the limit. Output lies in closed B_(2R+T), where chi=1 on a neighbourhood, for both entries. Thus D_chi A=A=A D_chi at every r.
